title: On-Site Phlebotomy and Occupational Testing Services under Physician Client Accounts
content:
Two kinds of field service are tied to the class of Physician Client Accounts: placement of a laboratory phlebotomist in the organization's office, and the occupational testing services (employer drug-screen and pre-placement panels, chain-of-custody collection, and medical review officer review).

## Availability grid

| Account class | Laboratory phlebotomist placed in the office | Average daily draws needed for a placed phlebotomist | Employer drug-screen and pre-placement panels | Chain-of-custody collections | Medical review officer (MRO) review of non-negative drug tests included |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Independent Practice Client Account | No | 0 (not offered) | No | No | No |
| Group Practice Client Account | No | 0 (not offered) | No | No | No |
| Multispecialty Medical Group Account | Yes | 35 | No | No | No |
| Federally Qualified Health Center Account | No | 0 (not offered) | No | No | No |
| Hospital Outreach Reference Account | No | 0 (not offered) | No | No | No |
| Occupational Health Employer Account | No | 0 (not offered) | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Reading the grid

- Only the Multispecialty Medical Group Account offers an in-office phlebotomist, and the office must average 35 draws a day for one to be placed.
- Only the Occupational Health Employer Account can order employer drug-screen and pre-placement panels, have chain-of-custody collections, and has MRO review of non-negative drug tests included.
- A draw figure of 0 means the class does not offer a placed phlebotomist.

## Illustration (hypothetical offices)

A Multispecialty Medical Group office averaging 40 draws a day is above the 35 the class needs; one averaging 28 a day is below it. A Group Practice office of any size has no phlebotomist placement in its class.
